figures.caption: The caption behind the figure explains the measurement (warm isolated stages on the published diverted bank), names both series by device, states that the two devices make this a stage attribution rather than a speedup comparison, warns that the full Jacobian contains the booking tangent so the bars are not additive, and identifies the dotted line as the 0.5 ms H200 target with the read outside it. It does not merely repeat the figure's title.
figures.judged_image: image-0.png (1399x720 rendered PNG attached to this review)

rubric.contrast: defect: the green P100 value labels and bars are #2e8b57 on white, which measures 4.25:1 and falls just under the 4.5:1 threshold for 14 pt text; the grey baseline value labels (#666666, 5.74:1) and the black category labels (#52514E, 7.94:1) pass
rubric.data_ink: passes: two solid bar series and their printed values on white carry all the ink; no fill bands, no gradient, no third encoding competing with the magnitudes
rubric.decoration: passes: no gridlines, no background fill, top and right spines removed; the single dotted vertical rule at 0.5 ms is the step target the caption names, which is data rather than decoration
rubric.label_collision: passes: no category label, tick label, axis label or value label is clipped at the canvas edge or overlaps another label or a bar; the longest category name ('geometry tangent, one direction') fits inside the 0.33 left margin and the largest value label (5741) sits well inside the right limit
rubric.legibility: passes: ten stage rows, each carrying a grey H200 bar and a green P100 bar with the value printed at the bar end and a logarithmic x-axis labelled 'warm wall [ms]'; the stage ranking is read in one pass
rubric.table_form: passes: the figure carries a magnitude comparison of ten stages across two devices, which a bar chart sets out faster than a table; the evidence fragment prints the same numbers in two tables beneath it, so the figure is not standing in for tabular data

findings.summary: The figure draws a 'Jacobian, frozen geometry' row (124 ms baseline, 5347 ms on the P100) that neither table in docs/evidence/fragments/sub-millisecond-forward-path/bank-step-speed.html has a line for: the baseline table lists only 'Full Jacobian' at 143.03 ms and the fast-path table only 'Full Jacobian' at 5381.76 ms. A reader checking a number against the tables finds one bar they cannot look up, so the figure and its evidence disagree on how many stages were measured.

The bars are drawn on a logarithmic x-axis starting at 0.2, so bar length is not proportional to value. On the page the 'Jacobian, frozen geometry' bar (124 ms) and the 'whole step' bar (369 ms) differ by only about a tenth of a bar length while the values differ threefold, and the 'flux and booking' bar (5.08 ms) is drawn almost as long as the 'read' bar (35.87 ms). Every value is printed at its bar end, so no data are hidden, but a reader who compares lengths rather than reading the numbers reads a wrong ratio. A dot or lollipop mark, or a linear axis, would encode magnitude honestly.

The green P100 value labels are drawn in #2e8b57 on white, which measures 4.25:1 contrast: just below the 4.5:1 threshold that applies to 14 pt text. The grey baseline labels (#666666, 5.74:1) and the category labels (#52514E, 7.94:1) are comfortable. The values remain legible for most readers and are duplicated by the bar lengths, so this does not stop a reader; a darker green for the printed numbers would clear the threshold without changing the series colour.

The two series are told apart by hue alone: baseline grey #929292 and fast-path green #2e8b57 differ by only 1.36:1 in relative luminance, so a deuteranope reads both as mid greys and the colour key in the legend carries little for them. The consistent vertical order (baseline above, fast path below) and the printed values keep the figure usable, but a second cue — a hatch on one series or a direct series label — would make the mapping unambiguous for colour-blind readers.

The legend names the second series 'P100 fast path', and every green bar in the figure is fifteen times longer than its grey partner (5741 ms against 369 ms for the whole step). Read on its own, the legend turns a fallback-device stage attribution into what looks like a large regression on the fast path. The caption beneath resolves this correctly by naming the titan P100 fallback and saying the comparison is not a speedup, so a reader who reaches the caption is not misled; naming the device in the legend entry itself would stop the misreading for a reader who meets the figure in the index.
